statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail sits at the bottom of the watch band while two-way structure holds, and Stress stays elevated on a deepening long-end selloff.
recommendation: Thursday's opening gap was fully retraced and the index has returned above its prior close, so mean reversion is still functioning in both directions. Stress stays elevated because the 7-year auction cleared at a 33-year-high yield, the 30-year sits at a 2004 high and crude is up more than 3%. The narrow danger window covers the 19:45-20:15Z cash close and immediate post-close repricing. Tail remains below the block threshold.
headline: Nasdaq-100 edges back above its prior close after the weakest 7-year auction since 1993; Tail at the bottom of the watch band
body: NDX is 30,477.92, up 7.63 points or 0.03%, against a 30,470.29 prior close. The session opened at 30,225.19, based at 30,204.16, fully retraced the gap to a 30,529.35 high and has since settled back above the prior close. That 325-point range has been traded in both directions with completed retracements, and no new session extreme has printed in the last hour, which is the central reason Tail stays at the bottom of the watch band rather than rising. VIX is 15.61, up 2.84% but below its 16.57 session high. The stress backdrop is genuinely difficult. The Treasury sold roughly $44bn of 7-year notes at a 5.085% high yield, the highest since April 1993, tailing a 5.078% market yield with a 2.42 bid-to-cover against 2.50 last month and indirect bidders down to 57.2% from about 61%. The 30-year is near 5.48% and the 10-year near 5.18%, multi-decade highs, while the 2-year is close to 4.92%, so the curve is steepening on term premium rather than policy repricing. WTI is near $95.27, up 3.38% after a $97 spike, with Brent above $107. Today's US data added to the pressure: initial claims printed 197K against a 201K consensus, new home sales beat at 0.684M, and the Kansas City Fed manufacturing index came in well above forecast. Two single-name stories matter for index composition. Oracle fell around 4-5% after sending a force majeure notice to the Blue Owl-owned developer of its Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico, which weighs on AI-infrastructure sentiment. Separately, Reuters reported that US and Iranian negotiators in New York are exploring a phased deal under which Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and Washington would lift its economic blockade; the talks are preliminary and a former negotiator put pre-election odds near 30%. That is a two-sided catalyst rather than a directional one. Per the risk contract, a weak auction, a hawkish yield impulse and high-importance headlines raise Stress and inform Confidence; they do not establish Tail on their own. Tail would require observed persistent directional efficiency, shallow or failed retracements and a hold near session extremes. The long end repricing to a 33-year auction high without breaking the equity range is evidence against that path, not for it. Shared Finviz context was about 115 minutes old and partial at the cutoff, with its calendar and futures sections unavailable, so it was treated as stale supporting evidence only and current levels were taken from primary sources.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 published hours stayed inside a watch-band regime with one orange print. Tail ran 20-23 through Wednesday's late US session, eased to 17-19 across the Asian overnight as conditions normalised, then rebuilt through a trend-down European morning to a 25 peak at 09:00Z, the only BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES slot in the window. It has since oscillated between 19 and 24 across the US session without establishing a one-way path, printing 19 at 17:00Z and 21 at 18:00Z. Stress stepped up from the high 40s overnight to the mid 50s as the long-end selloff deepened, and Confidence held in a tight 85-88 band throughout. Dominant mode was mixed for most of the window, with normal across the quiet overnight and trend-down during the bond-driven European morning.
outlookSummary: The base case is continued two-way trade inside Thursday's 30,204-30,529 range. Conditional Tail is lifted one point to 21 for the 20:00Z cash close and immediate post-close repricing, the narrow danger window, then eases to 18-19 across the quiet US evening and Asian overnight where the published lookback repeatedly mean-reverted. It rebuilds to 20-22 into the European open, which carried this window's highest published Tail, and peaks at 24 in the 13:00Z slot where the 12:30Z Durable Goods release and the 13:30Z US cash open stack together. Conditional Tail then decays to 21-23 through the US afternoon as event dispersion resolves. No slot reaches the blocking threshold, because that would require observed shallow pullbacks, failed retracements or extreme-holding that cannot be established from this cutoff. Confidence steps down from 87 to 81 across the forecast as distance from the verified evidence base grows.
